audit.why: Aatrox out-trades a tank support through the whole lane and only evens out when Nautilus becomes a teamfight CC engine — consistent with 51.68% over 7,212 games.
audit.corrected: Kept; the cooldown that defines the punish window was added.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every stage said "punish him when his Q is down" without ever giving the number.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s. At rank 1 that is a 14-second window in which he has neither engage nor disengage — the concrete shape of your whole lane.
audit.corrected: early, mid, wants.you[0] and whys[3] now carry the 14s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The passive root was written as an "auto-attack root", and a whiffed hook was treated as a pure free window.
audit.why: Riot's text: Staggering Blow roots on his FIRST attack against a given target, so it is one root per target per cooldown, not a repeating threat. And Dredge Line "colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it" — a hook that misses you but catches a wall is mobility for him, not a punish window for you.
audit.corrected: early now names Staggering Blow, states the first-attack rule, and warns that a terrain hook repositions him.

edits.before: You edge Nautilus from Level 1 even before your Q pattern is online — your base damage and heal let you win short trades, though his Q (Dredge Line) hook can cancel your combo and his auto-attack root chunks you if you get careless. Sidestep the hook — it's a slow, telegraphed skillshot — and don't walk into his root range for CS. Hold Q for after he commits, and use minions as blockers so a whiffed Dredge Line strands him. You stay ahead here; his shield and CC slow you down but don't out-trade your damage.
edits.after: You edge Nautilus from level 1 even before your Q pattern is online — your base damage and heal win short trades, though Dredge Line (Q) can cancel your combo and Staggering Blow, the root on his first attack against you, chunks you if you get careless. Sidestep the hook; it is a slow, telegraphed skillshot on a 14s cooldown at rank 1. Use minions as blockers, but note a hook into terrain drags HIM to the wall, so a whiff is not always a free window. Hold Q until he commits.

edits.before: From Level 3-6 you own the matchup. Your three-cast Q plus E drain simply out-sustains and out-damages a tank support-class bruiser, and his shield from Titan's Wrath can't keep up with sweetspot knockups. Punish him every time his Q is on cooldown — that's a long window where he has no engage and no disengage. At 6, World Ender makes you nearly unkillable in the brawl: the heal amp shrugs off his all-in even through the root and ult.
edits.after: From level 3-6 you own the matchup. Your three-cast Q plus E drain out-sustains and out-damages him, and Titan's Wrath, a flat 12s shield, can't keep up with sweetspot knockups. Punish him every time Dredge Line is down — 14s at rank 1 is a long window with no engage and no disengage. At 6, World Ender's heal amp shrugs off his all-in even through the root and Depth Charge, so commit the moment the hook is gone and let the drain do the rest.

edits.before: Bait out his Q (Dredge Line) hook before committing
edits.after: Bait out the 14s Dredge Line hook before committing

edits.before: Trade with Titan's Wrath shield up and root you with W passive
edits.after: Trade behind the Titan's Wrath shield and root you on his first hit

edits.before: Levels 4-5 favour Aatrox as repeated sweetspots and lifesteal grind him down between his long Q cooldowns.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 favour Aatrox as repeated sweetspots and lifesteal grind him down between 14s Dredge Line cooldowns.

notes: Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived "grounding" flag Riot's description does not support (drag + slow only); no grounding claim was made in this slice.
